Dagny Ostrova

The Closing, 2387. Wick-tender on Lantern's axial lamp and Speaker for the Wick crews. Forty-one, widowed, dry as rust, good with her hands and better with a crowd than she wants to be. Indentured since nineteen.
Pim Ostrova
The Closing, 2387. Dagny's son, twelve. Quick, thin, collects bolts. Worships his uncle Kas.
Kas Ostrova

The Closing, 2387. Kasimir, Dagny's younger brother. Ice-hauler pilot on the Caul run, master of the battered hauler Magpie. Gambler, charmer, owes everybody. Loves his sister and nephew more than he can afford to.
Teodor Basu

The Closing, 2387. Comptroller of the Halden-Ash Sabra Concern. Fifty-two, precise, soft-spoken, a stammer that comes out under pressure. He designed the Tally that keys Lantern's air to its debt, and he has done something worse.
Ruth Achterberg
The Closing, 2387. Director of the Halden-Ash Company's Sabra Concern. Sixty. Not cruel for pleasure: she counts. Wears the Director's seal, a brass key-disk, on a chain at her throat.
Hale Varga
The Closing, 2387. Chief of Company Security on Lantern. Ex-Concord marine, broad, scarred, loyal to his men. His squad sealed something on Caul that he has not stopped thinking about.
Odile Marchbank

The Closing, 2387. Dockmaster of the Dock Ring and keeper of the Ardent Mercy's bell. Seventies, half-deaf, steady engraver's hands. Rings the bell for every death on Lantern and cuts the name into the bronze.
Joss Teague
The Closing, 2387. Wick crewman, Dagny's oldest friend on the spine. Big laugh, bad knees.
Lemuel Adeyemi
The Closing, 2387. A Gallery pump-fitter whose balance crosses the dimming line on the first page.
Tamsin Hask

The Owing, 311 AC. A cutter: salvage diver in the frozen, unlit Cold Wards, stripping copper and steel from dead sections. Twenty-four, hard, funny when she forgets not to be. Born owing, like everybody.
Agathe Hask
The Owing, 311 AC. Tamsin's mother. Former pump-hand, now dying of lung-rot. Proud. Keeps the family's chits in a tin.
Jory Hask
The Owing, 311 AC. Tamsin's brother, fifteen. A runner for anyone who pays. Light fingers.
Orrin Sallow
The Owing, 311 AC. A junior counter of the Counting House. Twenty-six, born in the Upper Wards to a minor counting family, believer in the Account's righteousness until he checks its arithmetic.
Imre Vosk
The Owing, 311 AC. Comptroller-General of the Count, the Counting House's ruling body. Soft voice, perfect manners, holds the Count key and the lists.
Wenna Blackwood
The Owing, 311 AC. Boss of the Salt, the smugglers who run ice off Caul outside the Tally. Sixty, one eye, a voice like a gravel chute.
Brother Lusk
The Owing, 311 AC. The Bailiff of the Count: Vosk's enforcer, in grey, with a docket-baton.
Ninian
The Owing, 311 AC. The last master Wickwright, keeper of the dying lamp. Very old, nearly blind from the light he has spent his life tending.
Corvin Saal
The Healing, 3089 CE. Lien adjuster for Brightwater Recovery, bonded to the firm since he was nine for his father's water debt. Forty-four. Good at his job, which is making people pay.
Fen Adaire

The Healing, 3089 CE. Provenance archivist; she reads old corporate records for a living. Twenty-nine. Owns, by family inheritance, a bronze ship's bell inscribed ARDENT MERCY, and wants to take it home to wherever home was.
Mabry Ode
The Healing, 3089 CE. Master of the Good Title. Sixty-three, gaunt, Throat-runner in her youth. Mortgaged her ship to Brightwater to make this run.
Quennell Haste
The Healing, 3089 CE. Junior partner of Brightwater Recovery, travelling with the claim. Courteous, tireless, legally exact.
Idris Kell
The Healing, 3089 CE. Sergeant of Brightwater's bailiffs aboard the Good Title. Professional, bored, dangerous.
Tol Brask
The Healing, 3089 CE. Engineer of the Good Title, Ode's man for twenty years. Talks to machines, not people.
Senna Hask
The Healing, 3089 CE. Reader of the Account on Lantern, who keeps the Tally in the Counting House.
